country.odd: Three of these car makers come from {value}. Which one doesn't?
country.match: Match each car maker to its country.

founded.sort: from the oldest to the newest, by the year they were founded
founded.shot: In what year was the car maker {label} founded?

rows.label: Stellantis
rows.hook: formed when two big automakers merged into one giant multi-brand group

rows.label: BMW
rows.hook: is known for the spinning-propeller badge on sporty, precision-engineered sedans and coupes

rows.label: BYD Auto
rows.hook: grew from a battery maker into one of the world's biggest sellers of electric cars

rows.label: Toyota
rows.hook: built its reputation on dependable, fuel-efficient cars that just keep running

rows.label: Ford Motor Company
rows.hook: put moving assembly lines to work so ordinary families could finally afford a car

rows.label: General Motors
rows.hook: grew into a sprawling empire of car brands under one big corporate roof

rows.label: Volkswagen
rows.description: German automotive brand; manufacturing subsidiary of Volkswagen Group
rows.hook: made its name with an affordable, air-cooled, rounded people's car that became a hippie icon

rows.label: Porsche
rows.description: German automobile manufacturer specializing in high-performance sports cars, SUVs and sedans, owned by Volkswagen AG
rows.hook: builds sleek rear-engined sports cars instantly recognizable by their curved silhouette

rows.label: Ferrari
rows.hook: races a prancing-horse emblem and builds some of the most coveted supercars on earth

rows.label: Geely
rows.hook: grew from a small workshop into a global automaker that also owns famous overseas sports car brands

rows.label: Honda
rows.description: manufacturer of automobiles, motorcycles, and power equipment
rows.hook: began by building small engines and motorcycles before becoming a top-selling carmaker

rows.label: Jaguar Cars
rows.hook: built elegant, wood-and-leather British luxury saloons with a leaping cat on the hood

rows.label: Škoda Auto
rows.description: automotive manufacturing subsidiary of Volkswagen Group
rows.hook: makes practical, value-priced family cars with a winged-arrow badge

rows.label: Volvo Cars
rows.hook: built its whole brand around pioneering seatbelts and crash safety

rows.label: Audi AG
rows.description: German automotive manufacturing subsidiary of Volkswagen Group
rows.hook: races four interlocking rings on sleek performance sedans and SUVs

rows.label: Kia
rows.hook: went from a budget also-ran to a design-award-winning maker of stylish, affordable cars

rows.label: Nissan
rows.hook: pioneered mass-market electric cars alongside its everyday sedans and SUVs

rows.label: Lexus
rows.description: Japanese brand of luxury vehicle owned by Toyota Motor Corporation
rows.hook: was launched as a quieter, more pampering luxury alternative to sportier rivals

rows.label: Mazda
rows.hook: is famous for a lightweight rotary engine that spins instead of pumping pistons

rows.label: Land Rover
rows.hook: built rugged, boxy off-roaders favored by explorers and royalty alike

rows.label: Chevrolet
rows.hook: puts a bowtie badge on affordable pickups, muscle cars, and family sedans

rows.label: Subaru
rows.hook: builds most of its lineup around all-wheel drive as standard, even on ordinary sedans

rows.label: Renault
rows.hook: builds affordable hatchbacks and also fields a famous yellow Formula 1 team

rows.label: Cadillac
rows.hook: puts a crest badge on plush, chrome-heavy full-size luxury sedans

rows.label: Saab Automobile
rows.hook: built quirky, aircraft-inspired sedans before shutting down for good

rows.label: Jeep
rows.hook: is famous for a boxy, go-anywhere off-road vehicle with round headlights and a seven-slot grille

rows.label: Koenigsegg
rows.description: Swedish manufacturer of high-performance sports cars
rows.hook: is a tiny Swedish outfit that hand-builds some of the fastest hypercars on the planet

rows.label: Lotus Cars
rows.description: British manufacturer of sports and racing cars
rows.hook: builds ultralight, nimble sports machines built around the idea that less weight beats more power

rows.label: Opel
rows.description: German automobile manufacturer, subsidiary of Stellantis
rows.hook: puts a lightning-bolt badge on practical everyday German hatchbacks and sedans

rows.label: Maserati
rows.hook: puts a trident badge on elegant Italian grand tourers

rows.label: Alfa Romeo
rows.hook: puts a winged serpent badge on passionate, sporty Italian sedans and coupes

rows.label: Suzuki Motor Corporation
rows.hook: is known for tiny, affordable city cars and off-road vehicles alongside its motorcycles

rows.label: Bentley
rows.hook: builds hand-crafted British luxury cars once famous for a matching aero engine business

rows.label: Dodge
rows.hook: is famous for loud, muscular performance sedans with a ram's-head badge

rows.label: Rolls-Royce Motor Cars
rows.hook: builds the ultimate whisper-quiet, handcrafted status-symbol luxury sedans

rows.label: Mitsubishi Motors
rows.hook: puts a three-diamond badge on rugged SUVs and everyday commuter cars

rows.label: Buick
rows.description: luxury car brand of General Motors
rows.hook: was long marketed as a quietly upscale, slightly older-skewing American luxury brand

rows.label: Mahindra & Mahindra
rows.hook: grew from a farm-tractor business into a major maker of SUVs and utility vehicles

rows.label: Vauxhall
rows.description: English car company, subsidiary of Stellantis
rows.hook: put a griffin badge on everyday British family cars for well over a century

rows.label: Citroën
rows.hook: is known for a double-chevron badge and famously soft, cloud-like ride comfort

rows.label: Fiat
rows.hook: is famous for tiny, cheerful city cars that made mobility affordable across a whole country

rows.label: Dacia
rows.description: brand and romanian car manufacturer from Renault
rows.hook: builds no-frills, budget-friendly cars aimed at value-conscious buyers

rows.label: SEAT
rows.description: Spanish automotive company based in Martorell, subsidiary of Volkswagen Group
rows.hook: puts a stylized S badge on sporty, youth-oriented hatchbacks

rows.label: Lincoln Motor Company
rows.description: luxury division of Ford Motor Company
rows.hook: was created as an upscale luxury badge for an American mass-market carmaker

rows.label: Isuzu
rows.hook: is best known for its tough diesel engines and rugged trucks

rows.label: Holden
rows.description: Australian subsidiary of General Motors, an automaker
rows.hook: built a once-beloved lion-badge muscle car before its home market production ended

rows.label: Alpine
rows.hook: built lightweight, nimble little sports cars famous on rally stages

rows.label: Lancia
rows.hook: built innovative, elegant Italian sedans once favored by heads of state

rows.label: Groupe PSA
rows.hook: was the parent group behind two rival French carmakers before it merged into a bigger conglomerate

rows.label: Daihatsu
rows.hook: specializes in small, fuel-sipping kei-class city cars

rows.label: DAF
rows.description: Netherlands branch of American manufacturer Paccar
rows.hook: is best known for building heavy-duty trucks rather than passenger cars

rows.label: AvtoVAZ
rows.hook: built the basic, boxy sedans that were once the default car of an entire nation

rows.label: KG Mobility
rows.hook: was long known by an older name tied to a construction and defense conglomerate
